seoTitle: Fix Instagram Established Presence Branded Content Error
metaDescription: Instagram's Established Presence check blocks branded content tools for new or low-activity accounts. Learn how to audit your status and request a review.
intro: If Instagram is flagging your account as ineligible for branded content because of an 'established presence' problem, it usually means the platform hasn't yet verified enough authentic activity on your profile. This guide explains what triggers the flag - new accounts, low followers, or inconsistent posting - and walks through the actual screens where the ineligible status shows up, so you know exactly what Instagram is objecting to before you try to fix it. You'll also see how to request a manual review once you've addressed the underlying issues.

steps.heading: Check your Branded Content status page
steps.body: From your professional dashboard, open the branded content tools section and look at the Status entry near the top. A red X next to "Ineligible" confirms the block is active on your account rather than being a temporary glitch. Below it sits a Support section with a Learn more link, which is Instagram's own explanation of the requirement — worth reading in full before you change anything, since it spells out what the platform is actually checking for.

image.caption: The Status screen showing Ineligible with a red X, alongside the Support and Learn more links for branded content requirements.

steps.heading: Read the 'unable to monetise' breakdown
steps.body: Tapping into the eligibility details brings up a screen headed "You're currently unable to monetise," which lists Branded content with its own red X and a section called Current policy violations. This is where Instagram breaks eligibility down by category — Partner Monetisation Policies, Content Monetisation Policies, and Community Standards — each with a count of open issues next to it. If Partner Monetisation Policies shows a nonzero count, that's the established presence flag specifically, separate from any content violation under Community Standards.

image.caption: The "You're currently unable to monetise" screen, breaking eligibility issues into Partner Monetisation Policies, Content Monetisation Policies, and Community Standards.

steps.heading: Confirm your account is set up as Professional
steps.body: Branded content tools only apply to Professional accounts, so check your profile is switched to Creator or Business rather than a personal account. A Professional profile shows post count, follower count, and following count right under your bio, along with Edit profile and Share profile buttons — this is also the view Instagram uses to judge activity level, so a profile with very few posts and followers is a visible signal working against you, not just a background check you can't see.

image.caption: A Professional account profile page, showing the post/follower/following counts and Edit profile controls that feed into Instagram's activity checks.

steps.heading: Build a consistent posting and engagement history
steps.body: Established presence is a pattern check, not a one-time hurdle, so the fix is rarely instant. Post original content regularly over several weeks rather than in a single burst, and engage genuinely with your own audience — replies, Stories, and consistent activity all read as signals of a real, ongoing account rather than one set up purely to unlock monetization tools. Avoid reposting or low-effort content during this window, since it can work against you if it trips Community Standards at the same time.

steps.heading: Resolve any listed policy violations first
steps.body: Go back to the Current policy violations screen and clear anything showing a nonzero count before requesting a review — Instagram won't reconsider an account with open violations regardless of how active it's become. Address each category listed, since a review request submitted while violations are still open typically comes back with the same ineligible result.

steps.heading: Request a manual review
steps.body: Once your account reflects consistent activity and the violations list is clear, use the Learn more or Support link from the Status screen to submit a manual review request. Instagram's automated systems re-check periodically on their own too, so if you don't see an option to request review immediately, maintaining the improved activity for a few more weeks is often enough to clear the flag without any manual action.

faq.question: How long does it take to fix an established presence problem on Instagram?
faq.answer: It depends on your account's history - Instagram is looking for a consistent pattern of authentic activity, so it can take anywhere from a few weeks to longer if your account is very new.

faq.question: Does follower count affect branded content eligibility?
faq.answer: A low follower count combined with inconsistent posting is one of the common reasons Instagram flags accounts as not having an established presence, as shown by the activity data displayed right on your profile.

faq.question: Do I need a Business or Creator account to use branded content tools?
faq.answer: Yes, switching to a Professional Creator or Business account is a prerequisite - branded content tools and the eligibility status screen aren't available on personal accounts at all.

faq.question: What's the difference between the established presence flag and a policy violation?
faq.answer: On the eligibility breakdown screen, established presence issues show up under Partner Monetisation Policies, while content-specific problems appear separately under Content Monetisation Policies or Community Standards - they need to be resolved independently.

faq.question: Can I appeal if I think Instagram made a mistake?
faq.answer: Yes, once you've reviewed your account status and cleared any listed violations, you can request a manual review from the Support section of the Status screen to have the ineligible status reconsidered.
